chunks: (Tell me) O fellow-prisoners, are a number of gods better, or one God omnipotent?
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Are the many gods better or the One God?' in Surah Yusuf?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this verse is often cited to highlight Prophet Yusuf’s (AS) intellectual engagement with his prison companions, emphasizing the logical superiority of Tawhid over polytheism. It underscores the concept of Allah’s absolute sovereignty (Al-Qahhar) as the ultimate criterion for worship, a theme central to Shia theological discourses on divine unity and prophetic wisdom.
